concepts.definition: The library object that lets you talk to the LCD. When you create it, you give the connection pins in the order RS, E, D4, D5, D6, D7.
concepts.example: LiquidCrystal lcd(12, 11, 5, 4, 3, 2); means RS = D12, E = D11, D4 = D5 ... D7 = D2.
concepts.pitfall: Writing the pin order so that it does not match the wires: the display stays blank or shows meaningless characters.

concepts.definition: Starts the display and tells it the number of columns and rows. It is called once inside setup().
concepts.example: lcd.begin(16, 2); means a display with 16 columns and 2 rows.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to call begin: the display is not started and no text appears.

concepts.definition: Moves the cursor; the next text starts from there. Counting starts from 0, and the column comes first.
concepts.example: lcd.setCursor(0, 1); goes to the start of the bottom row.
concepts.pitfall: Counting rows from 1 or mixing up the order of column and row.

concepts.definition: The pin that decides how visible the text is. It is usually adjusted with a potentiometer.
concepts.example: In the lab model, if V0 goes above about 1.6 V, the display looks blank.
concepts.pitfall: Never adjusting the contrast: the text may not be visible even when the backlight is on.

concepts.definition: The LCD does not automatically delete a character written in a box; new text is written over the old one.
concepts.example: If the display shows 250 and 7 is written in the same place, you see 750; adding spaces with lcd.print("7  ") solves this.
concepts.pitfall: Writing a number that has become shorter without clearing: the old digits stay on the display.

concepts.definition: With createChar you save your own 5x8-dot symbol in a slot from 0 to 7; you can have at most 8 symbols.
concepts.example: Defining a degree sign and writing it to the display with lcd.write(byte(0)).
concepts.pitfall: Not calling clear() or setCursor() after createChar: the text does not appear on the display.

quiz.prompt: The program says LiquidCrystal lcd(9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4);. Which Uno pin should the LCD's E pin be connected to?
quiz.explanation: The parameter order is RS, E, D4, D5, D6, D7. The second number is E, that is 8: the E pin connects to D8. D9 goes to RS, and D4 goes to the D7 pin.

quiz.prompt: After the command lcd.setCursor(5, 1);, lcd.print("Merhaba"); runs. Which column is the last letter of the text (a) in? (Columns start from 0.)
quiz.explanation: The text starts at column 5. Merhaba (hello) has 7 letters; they go into columns 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. The last letter is in column 11. So 5 + 7 − 1 = 11. The answer 12 comes from counting one column too many in 5 + 7.

The LCD does not delete the old character. After 250 is written, the cursor goes back to the start and 7 is written only into the first box: the boxes become 7, 5, 0 and you see 750. To see only 7, you need lcd.clear() or lcd.print("7  ").

options: The lcd.print command should be inside loop()
The pin order should not be RS, E, D4, D5, D6, D7
quiz.explanation: Creating the object does not start the display. lcd.begin(16, 2) must be called inside setup(). print() works inside setup() too; the include and the pin order are also correct.

quiz.prompt: The LCD's backlight is on but no text appears on the display; the wires and the code are correct. Which setting should you check first?
options: Contrast (the voltage on the V0 pin)
The colour of the backlight resistor
quiz.explanation: The backlight is independent of the text; whether the text shows depends on the contrast. If the V0 voltage is not right (in the lab, above about 1.6 V), the display looks blank. The baud rate is a serial communication setting and does not affect the LCD.
